assertion: Builder confidence in the single-family housing market fell four points to 25, according to the National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index.
speaker: CNBC
independent_value: NAHB: fell four points to 25, lowest since April 2012; Nov 2025 was 38
measure: NAHB housing market index builder sentiment

assertion: In November, 46% of builders reduced prices, the highest share in the post-Covid period. The share of builders using sales incentives also hit a post-Covid high of 68%. That was the 20th consecutive month in which at least 60% of builders used them.
speaker: CNBC

assertion: The average rate on the 30-year fixed hit 7.51% on Monday, according to Mortgage News Daily. Last year at this time it was 6.38%.
speaker: CNBC
independent_value: MND Nov 16 7.51%; year-ago MND figure not independently verified, Freddie Mac 6.24% Nov 13 2025 is a different survey
sql: select date,value from econ.fred_indicators where series='MORTGAGE30US'

assertion: Mortgage rates pulled back slightly in October, but surged higher again last week.
speaker: CNBC
inaccuracy: The claim says rates pulled back in October; Freddie Mac shows them rising from 7.28 to a 7.40 peak mid-October before easing. MND daily series not checked
sql: select date,value from econ.fred_indicators where series='MORTGAGE30US'

assertion: Stepped-up immigration enforcement is keeping legal workers off job sites, deepening labor shortages and driving up costs. Higher fuel prices are prompting subcontractors to raise their rates sharply, and with fewer buyers in the market, more builders are scaling back construction.
speaker: Bill Owens (NAHB Chairman)
reason: No independent data on enforcement-driven labor effects or subcontractor rates was found; NAHB's own chief economist words it more mildly (enforcement 'is affecting labor availability in some markets'; fuel prices 'prompting subcontractors to raise their rates', without 'sharply'), and the HMI measures builder sentiment, not labor causes.
measure: NAHB housing market index builder sentiment

assertion: Mortgage rates above 7%, softer consumer confidence and an uncertain economic outlook are holding buyers back.
speaker: Robert Dietz (NAHB chief economist)
inaccuracy: The claim says rates above 7% are holding buyers back; rates were above 7% (Freddie Mac 7.11 to 7.40 since Oct 1, MND 7.46-7.51) but the causal link rests only on the buyer-traffic index falling to 16, not independent evidence
sql: select date,value from econ.fred_indicators where series='MORTGAGE30US'
